sector_model: Medical device, single-product (hypoglossal nerve stimulation for sleep apnea): US reimbursement and CPT coding drive revenue; SBC is large relative to cash flow; adjusted metrics exclude SBC, so GAAP and after-SBC cash flow are the primary lens.
thesis: Inspire Medical Systems (NYSE: INSP). Q3 2026 release (8-K 2026-11-02, Ex 99.1 read in full): revenue 206.7M, down 7.9% from 224.5M, attributed to lower US revenue from coding and reimbursement challenges; gross margin 86.0%; GAAP operating loss 28.7M; net loss 24.4M (EPS -0.84); adjusted EBITDA 37.9M (18.3%). 9M revenue 611.9M (-4.8%), net loss 35.4M. FY26 revenue guide narrowed to 850M to 860M (from 835M to 875M), adjusted EPS 1.20 to 1.40, GAAP EPS -0.36 to -0.10. Cash and investments 453.1M, no debt. AMA CPT panel approved a Category I code for single-lead HGNS effective 2028-01-01. TTM (FY25 + 9M26 - 9M25, XBRL): revenue 880.9M, net income 100.7M (FY25 was 145.4M; the TTM is positive only because of a strong H1 2025 comparison base effect, 9M26 is a loss), OCF 135.0M, capex 37.1M, FCF 97.9M, SBC 116.8M so FCF after SBC -19.0M. Shares 28,941,555 (release) x close 59.41 = market cap 1719M; TTM P/E 17.1x (not meaningful because earnings are falling), FCF yield 5.7% before SBC and negative after SBC; EV about 1266M = 1.44x TTM revenue. Close 59.41 is the lowest in the two month table seen (high close 76.78 on 2026-09-18); a price below a prior high is not evidence of cheapness.
counterthesis: Revenue is shrinking after reimbursement and coding disruption, GAAP operating income has turned negative, and FCF is only positive before 117M of SBC, so owners are not yet earning a cash return. The market may be right that the competition or coding problem is structural; the new CPT code does not start until 2028. Adjusted EPS excludes SBC, which is about 13% of TTM revenue. The 10-Q MD&A, risk factors, competitor (e.g. Nyxoah, LivaNova) and GLP-1 demand effects, inventory and receivables were not read; the 13G/A flurry 11-09 to 11-16 was not read (could be holder sales).
invalidation: Thesis of a recoverable franchise fails if US revenue keeps falling past FY26 guidance (below 850M), gross margin drops below 83%, cash burn after capex turns negative, or reimbursement problems persist beyond the 2028 CPT effective date.
